title: Transformations of Functions
seo_title: Precalculus Transformations of Functions Worksheets (TEKS P.2G)
standard_text: P.2G graph functions, including exponential, logarithmic, sine, cosine, rational, polynomial, and power functions and their transformations, including af(x), f(x) + d, f(x − c), f(bx) for specific values of a, b, c, and d, in mathematical and real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets on transformations of functions for Texas TEKS P.2G: shifts, stretches, reflections, f(bx), moving points and matching graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: f(x − c) + d: right c, up d.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • f(x) + d: up d. f(x − c): right c.
  • af(x): vertical stretch by |a|; a negative a reflects over the x-axis.
  • f(bx): divide every x-coordinate by b; a negative b reflects over the y-axis.
  • A point (x, y) on f moves to (x ÷ b + c, ay + d) on g(x) = af(b(x − c)) + d.

Examples

Example

g(x) = −2f(x + 3) + 1; (4, 5) on f

x: 4 − 3 = 1

y: −2(5) + 1 = −9

Answer: (1, −9)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Shifting the wrong wayf(x + 3) moves left 3.
Multiplying by bf(2x) halves the x-coordinates.
The wrong axis−f(x): x-axis. f(−x): y-axis.

faq.q: In what order do you apply transformations?
faq.a: Stretches and reflections first, then shifts.

faq.q: Does f(x) + d change the domain?
Does f(x − c) change the range?

items.q: Describe how the graph of g(x) = (x − 1)² + 2 is related to the graph of the parent function f(x) = x².
items.e: Inside the function, (x − 1) moves the graph the opposite way: right 1. Outside, +2 moves it up. Shift right 1, up 2.

sets.title: Stretches by b and exponential and log shifts

items.q: How is the graph of g(x) = √(3x) related to the graph of f(x) = √x?
c: Vertical shrink by a factor of 13
Horizontal shrink by a factor of 13
Horizontal stretch by a factor of 3
items.e: Replacing x with bx changes the graph sideways: every x-coordinate is divided by b = 3. Horizontal shrink by a factor of 13.

items.q: The point (4, 4) is on the graph of f(x) = |x|. Which point is on the graph of g(x) = |13x|?
items.e: g(12) = f(13 · 12) = f(4) = 4. Divide the x-coordinate by 13 and keep the y-coordinate. (12, 4).

items.q: The point (1, 1) is on the graph of f(x) = x3. Which point is on the graph of g(x) = (12x)3?
items.e: g(2) = f(12 · 2) = f(1) = 1. Divide the x-coordinate by 12 and keep the y-coordinate. (2, 1).

items.q: The point (1, 1) is on the graph of f(x) = √x. Which point is on the graph of g(x) = √(12x)?
items.e: g(2) = f(12 · 2) = f(1) = 1. Divide the x-coordinate by 12 and keep the y-coordinate. (2, 1).

items.q: The point (−8, −2) is on the graph of f(x) = ∛x. Which point is on the graph of g(x) = ∛(13x)?
items.e: g(−24) = f(13 · −24) = f(−8) = −2. Divide the x-coordinate by 13 and keep the y-coordinate. (−24, −2).

items.q: The point (4, 2) is on the graph of f(x) = √x. Which point is on the graph of g(x) = √(−x)?
items.e: g(−4) = f(−1 · −4) = f(4) = 2. Divide the x-coordinate by −1 and keep the y-coordinate. (−4, 2).

items.q: The point (2, 8) is on the graph of f(x) = x3. Which point is on the graph of g(x) = (2x)3?
items.e: g(1) = f(2 · 1) = f(2) = 8. Divide the x-coordinate by 2 and keep the y-coordinate. (1, 8).
